minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard Monty Tech's FY23 assessment, set to skip a capital planning session, and reviewed the draft warrant.
minutes.summary: A special virtual Finance Committee meeting heard Monty Tech's business director present its preliminary FY23 budget and how the state formulas drive Lunenburg's assessment. The finance director read the second-quarter FY22 revenue and spending summary. Members reviewed the draft town meeting letter and warrant, committee reports, and plans for the March 31 public hearing. Only adjournment was voted.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted on nothing but adjournment at a special virtual meeting, and no budget or warrant article was acted on.
Monty Tech's business director presented the preliminary FY23 budget and how state formulas drive Lunenburg's assessment, including use of excess and deficiency to lower assessments.
The finance director read the second-quarter FY22 revenue and spending summary; state aid and spending were each reported at about half.
Members generally agreed not to hold a discussion with the capital planning committee at the March 31 public hearing.
The town manager is to send an updated draft warrant, with recommendation votes expected March 31; a regular meeting is planned for April 14.

why_it_matters: Most of Lunenburg's Monty Tech assessment is a state-set minimum contribution that the school cannot control, so that part of the bill moves with the formula rather than with local choices.

The warrant articles that Finance Committee recommends on March 31 are the ones residents will be asked to vote on at town meeting, including a separate money article for the old primary school teardown.
watch_next: March 31 public hearing, where recommendation votes on the warrant are expected.
April 14 regular meeting, which the chair says could serve as a second public hearing if needed.
